When edge 5 is absent, edge 4 is the only learnable path into the output, so a conv there matters much more.
Removing edge 5 when edge 4 is already none cuts off every conv path to the output.
Removing edge 4 when edge 5 is none leaves the output fed only by edge 3, which badly degrades the cell.
Without a direct input-to-output skip, a skip on edge 0 provides a useful identity path instead of displacing a conv.
Without the edge-3 residual, a skip from the input to node 2 restores gradient flow, so it hurts less or helps.
A skip into the output node partly substitutes for the missing edge-3 residual.
Without the edge-3 shortcut, an identity path into the output is valuable rather than a loss of conv capacity.
Filling the empty direct input-to-output edge adds a short path, a bigger gain than replacing an existing skip there.
Without the edge-3 shortcut the output depends more on the deep paths, so strengthening edge 5 gains more.

raw:
The hypotheses below come from contrasts in the 100 measurements, mostly single matched parent pairs, plus general NAS-Bench-201 patterns. No new experiments were run. Most rest on one pair, so treat them as plausible rather than confirmed.

**Main patterns:**

- **Edge 3 is the cell's main residual path.** When edge 3 is `none`, many edits score higher:
  - `skip_connect` on edges 0, 1, 4 and 5 (pairs 65/66, 67/68, 63/64, 59/60).
  - `nor_conv_3x3` on edges 3 and 5 (pairs 83/84, 81/82).
  - One edit runs the other way: `skip_connect` on edge 2 was worse when edge 3 was `none` (61/62). It is not in the list.
- **Edges 4 and 5 are the two ways into the output node.** When one is `none`, the other edge matters much more:
  - Adding a conv there gains more (37/38).
  - Removing it costs much more (69/70, 72/73).
- **Replacing a conv with a conv gains little.** Turning edge 5 from `nor_conv_1x1` into `nor_conv_3x3` was slightly negative on all three datasets (case 12). The same edit from other edge-5 operations was clearly positive (cases 1, 10, 11).

**Caveat:** in cells made of only pooling or only skip edges, adding a skip on edge 3 hurts (cases 19, 20). This is why I left out the hypothesis "edge 3 → skip is higher when edge 3 is none."
